X_train.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns.tolist() num_vars.remove('Year_Built') num_vars.remove('Gr_Liv_Area') cat_vars = X_train.select_dtypes(include=['object', 'category']).columns.tolist() cat_vars.remove('Overall_Cond') knn_impute_vars = ['Year_Built', 'Gr_Liv_Area'] ordinal_vars = ['Overall_Cond'] ``` ::: ## Define Preprocessing: Base Pipelines ::: {#fe86e65c .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Create specific pipelines for different variable types knn_impute_pipe = Pipeline([ ('imputer', KNNImputer(n_neighbors=5)) ]) mean_impute_pipe = Pipeline([ ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='mean')) ]) median_impute_pipe = Pipeline([ ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')) ]) ordinal_pipe = Pipeline([ ('ordinal', OrdinalEncoder(categories=[qual_levels])) ]) ``` ::: ## Define Preprocessing: Base Pipelines ::: {#ff977045 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Linear regression categorical pipeline (drop='first' avoids collinearity) lm_cat_pipe = Pipeline([ ('rare_label', RareLabelEncoder(tol=0.01, n_categories=1, replace_with='Other', missing_values='ignore')), ('one_hot', OneHotEncoder(drop='first', sparse_output=False, handle_unknown='ignore')) ]) # KNN categorical pipeline (no drop, need scaling) knn_cat_pipe = Pipeline([ ('rare_label', RareLabelEncoder(tol=0.01, n_categories=1, replace_with='Other', missing_values='ignore')), ('one_hot', OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False, handle_unknown='ignore')) ]) ``` ::: ## Assembling Column Transformers for LM {.smaller} ::: {#2f7e187f .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} lm_knn_impute_ct = ColumnTransformer(transformers=[ ('knn_impute', knn_impute_pipe, knn_impute_vars), ('ordinal', ordinal_pipe, ordinal_vars), ('cat', lm_cat_pipe, cat_vars) ], remainder='passthrough') lm_mean_impute_ct = ColumnTransformer(transformers=[ ('mean_impute', mean_impute_pipe, knn_impute_vars), ('ordinal', ordinal_pipe, ordinal_vars), ('cat', lm_cat_pipe, cat_vars) ], remainder='passthrough') lm_median_impute_ct = ColumnTransformer(transformers=[ ('median_impute', median_impute_pipe, knn_impute_vars), ('ordinal', ordinal_pipe, ordinal_vars), ('cat', lm_cat_pipe, cat_vars) ], remainder='passthrough') ``` ::: ## Assembling Column Transformers for KNN {.smaller} Notice we also need to Standardize all variables for KNN. ::: {#8d86622c .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} knn_knn_impute_ct = ColumnTransformer(transformers=[ ('knn_impute', knn_impute_pipe, knn_impute_vars), ('ordinal', ordinal_pipe, ordinal_vars), ('cat', knn_cat_pipe, cat_vars) ], remainder='passthrough') knn_mean_impute_ct = ColumnTransformer(transformers=[ ('mean_impute', mean_impute_pipe, knn_impute_vars), ('ordinal', ordinal_pipe, ordinal_vars), ('cat', knn_cat_pipe, cat_vars) ], remainder='passthrough') knn_median_impute_ct = ColumnTransformer(transformers=[ ('median_impute', median_impute_pipe, knn_impute_vars), ('ordinal', ordinal_pipe, ordinal_vars), ('cat', knn_cat_pipe, cat_vars) ], remainder='passthrough') ``` ::: ## "Workflow Sets" in Python {.smaller} - `scikit-learn` does not have an exact equivalent to `workflow_set`. - The most standard Python approach is: 1. Create un-fitted Pipeline objects blending transformers and models. 2. Store them in a dictionary mapping `model_name -> Pipeline`. 3. Iterate over the dictionary, evaluating each via `cross_validate`. ::: {#792f7dbe .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} workflows = { # Linear Regression "lm_knn_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', lm_knn_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('model', lm_model)]), "lm_mean_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', lm_mean_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('model', lm_model)]), "lm_median_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', lm_median_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('model', lm_model)]), # KNN 5 "knn5_knn_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', knn_knn_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('scale', StandardScaler()), ('model', knn5_model)]), "knn5_mean_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', knn_mean_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('scale', StandardScaler()), ('model', knn5_model)]), "knn5_median_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', knn_median_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('scale', StandardScaler()), ('model', knn5_model)]), # KNN 10 "knn10_knn_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', knn_knn_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('scale', StandardScaler()), ('model', knn10_model)]), "knn10_mean_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', knn_mean_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('scale', StandardScaler()), ('model', knn10_model)]), "knn10_median_impute": Pipeline([('preproc', knn_median_impute_ct), ('nzv', VarianceThreshold()), ('scale', StandardScaler()), ('model', knn10_model)]) } ``` ::: ## Fit Resamples {.smaller} Now we map `cross_validate` across our dictionary of models: ::: {#a50ae1c2 .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} results = [] for name, wf in workflows.items(): cv_res = cross_validate(wf, X_train, y_train, cv=ames_folds, scoring=['neg_root_mean_squared_error', 'r2']) # Average across folds rmse = -cv_res['test_neg_root_mean_squared_error'].mean() r2 = cv_res['test_r2'].mean() results.append({'wflow_id': name, 'rmse': rmse, 'rsq': r2}) results_df = pd.DataFrame(results).sort_values(by='rmse') ``` ::: ## View Metrics ::: {#bdc88578 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} show(results_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

{.smaller} - How do we choose what variables to include in our model? - Up to now... include all of them... probably not the best - Advantage of linear regression: interpretability - Including every feature decreases interpretability - Reasons for feature selection: + Improve model performance + Improve model interpretability - Parsimony: simpler models are called more *parsimonious* - Occam's Razor: more parsimonious models are better than less parsimonious models, holding all else constant ## Types of feature selection - Subset selection: Forward/Backward/Best-Subset Selection - Shrinkage-based methods: LASSO and Ridge Regression - Dimension reduction: consider linear combinations of predictors # Subset Selection ## Exercise - With your group, write out the steps for the following algorithms on the board + Group 1: Forward selection + Group 2: Backward elimination + Group 3: Step-wise selection + Group 4: Best-subset selection ## Subset Selection in Python {.smaller} - `scikit-learn` provides an implementation for Forward/Backward Sequential Feature Selection: `SequentialFeatureSelector` - Also provides `SelectKBest`, `SelectFromModel`, `RFE` (Recursive Feature Elimination). - regularization (shrinkage-based) methods almost always perform better computationally and prediction-wise than exhaustive best-subset. ## Feature Selection via Sequential Feature Selector ```python from sklearn.feature_selection import SequentialFeatureSelector sfs = SequentialFeatureSelector(lm_model, n_features_to_select='auto', direction='forward', # or 'backward' cv=5) sfs.fit(X_train_transformed, y_train) # Which features were selected? sfs.get_support() ```
